summary: Built 1934 in George Washington State Forest, moved to Escoheag Hill in 1937-38; the moved structure stands unmaintained with its wooden cab burned.

facts.design: Steel tower: 65 ft per FFLOS for the original; NHLR gives 80 ft, modified Aermotor, for the moved Escoheag Hill structure
facts.status_note: The original George Washington site is gone. The tower was moved to Escoheag Hill, where the steel structure stands unmaintained and its wooden cab was burned.
facts.agency: Rhode Island Department of Environmental Management (administers the Escoheag Hill structure)

events.note: First operated 1934 on an unnamed knoll inside the George Washington State Forest; a 1934 annual report quoted by Forest Lookouts says it was built at federal expense as a work project
A 1937 study said the tower would move to Escoheag Hill; NHLR says it was moved in 1937
FFLOS says moved to Escoheag in 1938; NHLR says it was rebuilt at its present location in 1938. Sources disagree on the move year

Break-in at the tower on Escoheag Hill (not the original site), reported in a Newport Mercury report dated March 21, 1952, as quoted by Forest Lookouts. The report says forest service staff found it 'yesterday', so the discovery date itself is not given. Stove, generator, telephone and other equipment stolen; map table smashed
Not an active lookout since around 1990 (NHLR, approximate); refers to the Escoheag Hill structure
Non-standard wooden cab burned by vandals sometime after 2009; exact year not given. Destroyed most upper landings and damaged the upper stairs

notes_for_editor: Unresolved: (1) move year: FFLOS says moved to Escoheag in 1938, NHLR says moved 1937 and rebuilt 1938; story reports both. (2) Height: FFLOS '65 ft' for the original tower vs NHLR '80ft' for the Escoheag structure it traces to the same 1934 build; not reconciled. (3) Brief record status 'gone' is right for the original George Washington site only; the structure stands at Escoheag Hill, so the record is not wrong but a visitor could misread it. No correction proposed. (4) The 1952 break-in is at Escoheag Hill, not at the original site; its only source is a Forest Lookouts page quoting the Newport Mercury, not the clipping itself. (5) FFLOS registers a separate 'Escoheag Tower Site' (US 1585, RI 12) about half a kilometre from the NHLR coordinates; it lists abandoned remains on site while NHLR lists a standing structure. Likely the same structure catalogued twice, not confirmed. (6) Not read: the Valley Breeze CCC article used in the existing us-ri-escoheag-hill story (it places the first tower in Glocester as the 'George Washington Memorial Fire Tower'); this run stayed within its page-read budget, so the Burrillville-vs-Glocester dispute is left to that story. (7) No staffing history for the original tower in any source read, so none is stated.
